TensorRT plugin issues found with Volta
=======================================

Sources: TensorRT OSS at 7fe18f08 (main, 2026-11-27; external/ptx/sources/frameworks.txt),
fetched into target/ptx-sources/TensorRT by external/ptx/extraction/fetch_sources.py. The
plugin units compile for sm_100a (nvcc 13.2, C++20) with external/ptx/extraction/survey.py;
each case of external/ptx/TensorRT/cases.py launches one kernel as the plugin's host code does:

    uv run external/ptx/extraction/survey.py TensorRT
    python3 external/ptx/verify.py TensorRT

Volta treats floats as exact reals, so nothing below is a rounding difference. Volta runs one
CTA per case (its `cta`), so a race between two CTAs is out of its reach.


1. Reported by Volta
--------------------

TRT-1  DisentangledAttention (DeBERTa): a partial 64 x 64 tile writes past its rows (race,
       wrong output, out-of-bounds accesses)
Where:    plugin/disentangledAttentionPlugin/disentangledKernel.cu:84,
          GatherAddGatherTransposeAddMul_fused; launched by
          DisentangledAttentionPlugin::enqueueType (disentangledAttentionPlugin.cpp:249) with
          grid ((S - 1) / 64 + 1, (S - 1) / 64 + 1, BH) and block (64, 4).
Volta:    disentangled_s40_partial_tile (BH = 2, S = 40, span 128): REJECTED, memory-conflict
          freedom: WriteWrite on result[40] (and on the elements S apart after it) between
          thread 40 (row j = 0, column k = 40) and thread 64 (row 1, column 0), both at
          `st.global.b32` of the result write. With one head
          (disentangled_s40_partial_tile_one_head) the run stops at an out-of-bounds read
          of data2 (row 40 of 40). S = 64 is proved equal to its spec on all 4,096 outputs
          (ACCEPT), and S = 128 verifies.
What:     The grid rounds S up to whole 64 x 64 tiles, and the kernel has no bounds check:
          every thread gathers data2 into the shared tile, reads data0 and data1 and writes
          result at IND(i, j, k) = (i * S + j) * S + k, for j and k up to the tile's end.
          When S is not a multiple of 64, a thread with k >= S writes the element (j + 1,
          k - S) that another thread also writes, with a different value, and a thread with
          j >= S writes into the next head's rows, or, for the last head, past the result.
          Which write lands depends on scheduling, so the output changes from run to run.
          The plugin accepts any S (supportsFormatCombination and configurePlugin check only
          types, formats and ranks).
Fix:      skip the out-of-range threads: guard the data2 gather and tile store by
          `j + ty < S && k < S`, and the data0/data1 reads and the result write by the same
          bound (external/ptx/TensorRT/units/disentangledKernel_fixed.cu).
Status:   the fixed kernel is proved equal to the spec at S = 40 (ACCEPT, 1,600 outputs) and
          race free at S = 40 with two heads and at S = 100 (block (1, 1, 1)). Upstream,
          NVIDIA/TensorRT#4005 (open since 2024-07) reports DeBERTa outputs that change from
          run to run with this plugin at a dynamic sequence length of 4059, not a multiple of
          64, with no diagnosis; this is a likely cause. Reported as NVIDIA/TensorRT#4957 (2026-11-27).

TRT-2  ScatterND: the transformed indices are written past the plugin's workspace for a data
       tensor of rank 3 or more (out-of-bounds write)
Where:    plugin/scatterPlugin/scatterLayer.cu:86, scatterNDInference:
          `int* wo = (int*)(workspace); int* transformedIdx = wo + sizeof(int)*nOutputDims;`,
          then transformIdxKernel<<<nRows, 1>>>(transformedIdx, ...) at :89. The workspace is
          `outputs[0].dims.MAX_DIMS * sizeof(int32_t) + nSlices * sizeof(int32_t)` bytes
          (scatterPlugin.cpp:101), and nOutputDims is the data tensor's rank
          (scatterPlugin.cpp:210).
Volta:    scatternd_rank4_indices_past_workspace (data rank 4, 3 slices of index rank 2, the
          workspace at 0x40000, 44 bytes): ABORT, out-of-bounds Global store at 0x40040, the
          first transformed index. Rank 2 (scatternd_rank2_indices) and the corrected offset
          (scatternd_rank4_indices_fixed) verify.
What:     `wo` is an int*, so `wo + sizeof(int) * nOutputDims` advances 4 x rank ints, 16 x
          rank bytes, while the workspace reserves 8 ints (32 bytes) for the coefficients.
          From rank 3 the nSlices indices start past those 32 bytes and their last 16 x rank -
          32 bytes lie past the workspace's end, over whatever TensorRT placed after it.
          Ranks 1 and 2 stay in bounds, leaving a gap.
Fix:      `int* transformedIdx = wo + nvinfer1::Dims::MAX_DIMS;`, the layout the workspace size
          assumes (or `wo + nOutputDims`).
Status:   the corrected offset verifies. Reported as NVIDIA/TensorRT#4958 (2026-11-27); no
          earlier report.


TRT-3  EfficientNMS: an iteration's lead thread rewrites the shared `blockState` before the
       other threads have read the previous iteration's (race, wrong suppression)
Where:    plugin/efficientNMSPlugin/efficientNMSInference.cu:223-336, EfficientNMS<T, Tb>; launched
          by EfficientNMSLauncher (:340) with one block of numSelectedBoxes / 5 threads (819 for
          the default 4096; 256 or 512 for small values) per image.
Volta:    efficient_nms_40_boxes (40 candidates, 20 coinciding pairs, defaults otherwise):
          REJECTED, memory-conflict freedom: ReadWrite on `blockState` between thread 0's read in
          iteration 0's IoU loop (`blockState == 1`, PTX line 1500) and thread 1's
          `blockState = -1` as iteration 1's lead (line 1388), and WriteRead between that write
          and threads 2 and 3's reads of iteration 0's value. Also with 24 candidates in one
          warp (efficient_nms_24_boxes_one_warp): since Volta (sm_70) a warp's threads are not
          implicitly synchronized either.
What:     Each iteration i has one __syncthreads (:291): before it, iteration i's lead thread
          writes blockState (-1 skip, -2 exit, 1 suppress); after it, every thread reads
          blockState in its IoU test. Nothing orders those reads before iteration i + 1's lead
          writes blockState again, before the next barrier. A thread still in iteration i that
          reads the new value skips suppressing against box i (-1), returns early (-2), or
          suppresses against a box that was dropped (1), so the detections depend on scheduling.
          Reachable with the defaults whenever more than one thread is active, i.e. always.
Fix:      a barrier at the start of each iteration, before the lead's write
          (external/ptx/TensorRT/units/efficientNMSInference_fixed.cu).
Status:   the fixed kernel verifies with 40 and with 24 candidates, and keeps the 20 even boxes
          with their scores. Not reported upstream that we could find.

2. Kernels Volta checked without findings
-----------------------------------------

Race free (graph checks) and, where named, proved equal to a spec on every output (ACCEPT):
skipLayerNorm (skipLayerNormKernelSmall and skipLayerNormKernel, f32 and f16, ACCEPT; skipln_vec
at 768, race free: its proof takes past the 10-minute timeout), embLayerNorm (fixed and
variable sequence lengths, HFace and MTron; no spec, as a PTX spec cannot read the token ids'
integers), the BERT mask kernels (maskIdxKernel{,Small}, fillSBSMaskKernel), the batched
transpose (ACCEPT), groupNorm's scale-shift (ACCEPT), PointPillars' scatterBEV and ScatterND's
index transform at rank 2. Volta checks one CTA per case, so each spec case launches a shape
whose output one block writes.

Leads from reading the code that Volta does not reproduce yet (they need atomic operations
Volta does not model): voxelGenerator's generateFeatures_kernel stores center.z at
`pillarOutSM[p][pt][warp_size + 5]` (voxelGeneratorKernels.cu:242) instead of index 10,
overwriting feature 4 of point pt + 3 and leaving feature 10 unwritten; generateVoxels_kernel
reads `points_size[B]` past the batch for the rounded-up grid's tail threads (:35-42).


3. Volta changes these kernels needed
-------------------------------------

- `cvt` with integer rounding (`.rni`, `.rzi`, `.rmi`, `.rpi`; PTX ISA 9.7.9.21), float to
  integer (clamped to the destination's range, so `.sat` is redundant) or to a float of the
  same size: exact on a concrete value, and an integer converted to a float rounds to that
  integer; any other symbolic value is unsupported (`LoweredInstr::CvtRoundInt`).
- `bmsk.{clamp,wrap}.b32` (9.7.1.22) over concrete operands (`LoweredInstr::Bmsk`).
- `set.CmpOp.dtype.stype` (9.7.6.1, 9.7.7.1): 1.0 or all ones where the comparison holds
  (`LoweredInstr::Set`).
- `atom` and `red` lower to `LoweredInstr::UnmodeledAtomic`: atomics are not modeled, so a
  run that executes one stops as unsupported, and a kernel whose launch never reaches one
  (EfficientNMS outside its ONNX-indices output) is analyzed in full.
Together these lower 321 of the 400 plugin kernels (196 before). What still stops the others:
`bar.red.{and,or}.pred` (56, `__syncthreads_and`/`_or` in the sorts and NMS), `cvt.pack.sat.s8`
(16, int8 quantization), relaxed loads and stores (9) and NaN literals (6).
